subject: Customer erase handshake: snapshots, backup policy constraints & next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Young <rachel.young@avasolutions.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up + clarify erase timeline for backups/snapshots (post-call)

Hi Rachel —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can get this scoped for legal and infra:

Key notes from our discovery:
- You need account-level RTBF capability for end-user records served through Redwood (customer IDs, chat transcripts, embeddings).
- Primary constraint: customer-managed snapshots and third-party backups are retained by your infra team (AWS snapshot lifecycle + vendor-managed vaults).
- Regulatory point: some EU-origin users must remain in EU region controls (data residency for storage and logs).

Questions to unblock scoping:
1) When you say "full purge" what is your required maximum SLA after a delete request reaches us? We heard 30 days as a possible maximum — can you confirm if you expect sub-72h or 30-day?
2) Do you treat cloud snapshots (EBS/EFS/S3 lifecycle) as in-scope for RTBF or are they a separate operational responsibility? If in-scope, who owns snapshot deletion (Ava infra / backup vendor)?
3) Are there legal-hold exceptions we should model (e.g., litigation holds that can pause purges for a set of users)? If yes, who issues holds (legal@avasolutions.com)?
4) Do you require a signed attestation/forensic report after purges (for audits)?

What Redwood can offer (high level):
- Soft-delete + background purge job that removes active store copies within 24–72 hours by default.
- Metadata tombstones retained to support audits and billing for up to 90 days (configurable).
- For backups/snapshots under Redwood-managed storage we can trigger deletion and provide a signed confirmation log. For third-party snapshots we can provide a coordination playbook and a signed handoff but cannot directly modify your vendor-managed snapshots without cross-account automation consent.

I attached a short matrix that maps purge SLA options to plan tiers and what we can guarantee for backups (erase_sla_matrix.xlsx).

Next steps: please confirm 1–4 above and, if helpful, loop in your infra contact (cc'd legal if holds are needed). Happy to schedule a 30-min session with Monica and Karthik to walk through the technical playbook.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: erase_sla_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 38KB)]

From: Rachel Young <rachel.young@avasolutions.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up + clarify erase timeline for backups/snapshots (post-call)

Hi Sean —

Appreciate the recap — this matches our notes. Quick answers inline: 

1) SLA: Our internal bar is 72 hours for removing primary (hot) copies after a verified delete request. We can accept up to 30 days for deep archival snapshots, but we need visibility and an attestation when the archival copy is destroyed.

2) Snapshots: Our backups are a mix — some are AWS-managed EBS snapshots tied to the instance lifecycle, some are kept by a third-party backup vendor (VaultCo). For EBS/EFS snapshots that are within our AWS account we expect Redwood to provide a mechanism to surface the references so our infra team can tie deletion to lifecycle policies. For VaultCo-managed vaults we need Redwood to hand over an ordered list of object identifiers and a recommended workflow; VaultCo will require a separate change request to delete.

3) Legal holds: yes, we have litigation and compliance holds issued by legal@avasolutions.com. Holds can apply at user, account, or org level and will pause purge flows until released.

4) Attestation: yes, we need an exportable audit record and a signed attestation for any archival deletion (VaultCo or deep backup).

Additional: We need confirmation that logs (access logs, model request traces) can be partitioned so EU-origin logs remain in EU.

Can Monica/Karthik propose the concrete steps you recommend for connecting Redwood deletion events to our S3/EBS lifecycle and VaultCo handoffs? Also please call out which options would require Dedicated or Private deployment (we're evaluating tradeoffs).

Thanks,
Rachel Young
Director, Security & Compliance | Ava Solutions

Subject: Re: Follow-up + clarify erase timeline for backups/snapshots (post-call)

Hi Rachel — thanks for the quick clarifications. Adding technical details so legal/infra can review quickly.

Short answers up front:
- Hot store: Redwood's default pipeline will remove active copies within 24–72 hours of validation.
- Backups/snapshots: behavior depends on where snapshots live.

Detailed behavior and options:
1) Redwood-managed storage (hosted API):
   - Soft-delete is immediate; background purge attempts to delete tombstoned data from active stores within 24–72 hours.
   - For snapshots Redwood created (rare, only for backup-enabled accounts) we can trigger snapshot deletion and provide a signed deletion log.

2) Customer-managed AWS snapshots (in your AWS account):
   - We can emit a verified-delete event with object references and timestamps to an S3 bucket or SNS topic you control. Your infra team can then run an automated lifecycle or lambda to remove snapshots.
   - We can sign and timestamp the event (PKI-backed) so VaultCo or your infra have an audit trail.

3) Third-party backups (VaultCo):
   - Redwood cannot directly delete objects in a vendor-managed vault unless you provide cross-account automation credentials and an agreed runbook.
   - Typical approach: Redwood provides an ordered list of identifiers + signed attestation; your ops team raises the change request with VaultCo. We can support a scripted handoff (API call payload) to accelerate deletion.

4) Legal holds:
   - We surface holds in the deletion workflow (API flag on delete request). When a hold is present we mark the user as "hold" and halt the purge pipeline; the request is recorded and can be released by legal.

5) EU logs/residency:
   - Redwood can partition logs and traces by region; EU-origin logs can remain in EU regions if you enable regional isolation under the Dedicated or Private options. The hosted plan can provide limited geo-partitioning but not the full residency guarantees required by some audits.

Timelines and options matrix:
- Default hosted: 24–72h hot purge; 90-day tombstone for audit metadata; backup coordination only (hand-off).
- Dedicated: same hot purge SLAs; can set automated cross-account snapshot deletion via secure automation (requires infra IAM roles); attestation available.
- Private: full on-prem/residency control; Redwood can run a direct purge job across customer-managed storage depending on networking and credentials.

Attachments: I attached the SLA matrix and a short sample delete-event payload for VaultCo.

Recommended next steps (for clarity and to keep vendor ops moving):
1) Ava infra: confirm if you want us to deliver delete events to an S3 bucket or an SNS webhook.
2) Legal: confirm attestation format (signed PDF + audit CSV) and acceptance criteria.
3) Ops: point us to VaultCo contact or provide a sample API endpoint for scripted handoffs.

I can run a 30-min technical walkthrough this week with Karthik to demo the event payload and show sample attestation logs.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Privacy Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
